metaData.originalTitle: Qwen-Image-Bench：56 个创作级考点，定义生图评测新标准！
metaData.title: Qwen-Image-Bench: 56 Creative Benchmarks Defining a New Standard for Image Generation Evaluation
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: Tongyi Lab introduces Qwen-Image-Bench, a set of 56 fine-grained creative benchmarks for text-to-image evaluation designed by a team of professional artists, along with the open-source automated evaluation model Q-Judger, aiming to bridge the evaluation gap between basic generation and professional creation.
metaData.summary: This article introduces Qwen-Image-Bench, the latest text-to-image evaluation benchmark released by Tongyi Lab. Developed with the participation of a team of professional visual and aesthetic design artists, this benchmark aims to address the issue that existing T2I evaluations only focus on basic semantic alignment and image quality, while ignoring the aesthetic intuition, world knowledge, and logical reasoning abilities required in real creative scenarios. Qwen-Image-Bench deconstructs creative ability into 5 core capability pillars and 17 typical creative scenarios, further refined into 56 quantifiable evaluation dimensions covering high-frequency real-world scenarios such as visual storytelling, brand design, game art, and comic creation. The benchmark includes 1000 bilingual (Chinese and English) hierarchical prompts, each precisely covering 4+ third-level dimension test points. Additionally, the article introduces the open-source automated evaluation model Q-Judger, whose evaluation results show significant correlation (Spearman 0.92) with professional assessments from senior human artists. Through multiple practical case comparisons, the article demonstrates the capability differences of various models in dimensions such as fashion styling, artistic style, product design, and game UI, pointing out that current T2I models have obvious gaps in subfields like text accuracy, information visualization, and cross-language generation, with world knowledge and logical reasoning abilities being the watershed that determines whether a model can enter the first tier.

mainPoints.point: Existing T2I evaluation standards cannot measure the true creative ability of models.
mainPoints.explanation: Current evaluations mostly focus on basic semantic adherence and image quality, ignoring the aesthetic intuition, world knowledge, and logical reasoning abilities required in professional creation scenarios, leading to poor performance of high-scoring models in actual advanced creation.

mainPoints.point: Qwen-Image-Bench deconstructs creative ability into 56 fine-grained test points.
mainPoints.explanation: Designed by a team of professional artists, covering 17 creative scenarios including visual storytelling, brand design, and game art, achieving multi-dimensional and quantifiable evaluation through 1000 hierarchical prompts, aiming to identify the strengths and weaknesses of different models.

mainPoints.point: The accompanying open-source automated evaluation model Q-Judger achieves efficient evaluation.
mainPoints.explanation: Q-Judger supports fine-grained scoring from 56 dimensions including image quality, aesthetics, and image-text consistency, with evaluation results highly correlated with human experts (Spearman 0.92), providing quantifiable closed-loop feedback for model optimization.

keyQuotes: When AI evolves from 'being able to generate images' to replacing professional photography and even deeply participating in artistic creation, how should we evaluate a model's 'true creative ability'?
Because 'high scores' do not equal 'good usability'.
'Drawing correctly' and 'drawing beautifully' are just the starting points; 'understanding creation' is the ultimate goal.

Top-tier models need to understand human creative needs and mobilize their own knowledge and logical reasoning abilities. Behind this lies the deep synergy of language understanding, knowledge integration, and the model's aesthetic sense and creative execution.

relatedArticles.title: OpenAI's Former CTO Brings a Prototype of an AI That Is Always 'Present' | Hao's Paper Talk
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth interpretation of the Interaction Model released by Thinking Machines. Starting from the three conditions of communication theory (co-presence, simultaneity, and concurrency), it analyzes the fundamental flaws of current AI interaction systems and elaborates on how the model achieves a truly 'present' next-generation human-computer interaction mode through 200ms micro-turn heartbeats, a unified multimodal architecture, and a dual-model design.

relatedArticles.title: GLM-5V-Turbo Released: A Multimodal Coding Foundation Model
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Zhipu AI has released GLM-5V-Turbo, a multimodal coding foundation model that supports native visual understanding and code generation, is deeply optimized for Agent scenarios, and offers a 200k context window.

relatedArticles.title: Wan2.7-Image: Enhanced Realism, Stable Text Rendering, and Precise Color Accuracy
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Tongyi Lab releases the Wan2.7-Image generation model, featuring significant improvements in character realism, text rendering stability, and color accuracy.

relatedArticles.title: Qwen3.7-Max Redefines the Foundation of AI Agents
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Alibaba Tongyi Lab releases Qwen3.7-Max, demonstrating long-horizon agent stability in extreme stress tests with 35 hours of continuous autonomous execution and 1,158 tool calls without interruption, achieving cross-framework generalization through a decoupled training architecture.

relatedArticles.title: 215 SOTA Benchmarks + Emergent Vibe Coding! Qwen3.5-Omni Released
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Tongyi Lab releases Qwen3.5-Omni, a native omni-modal large model that achieves SOTA in 215 benchmarks, supporting real-time audio-visual interaction, voice cloning, and emergent Vibe Coding capabilities.

relatedArticles.title: Qwen3.5 Small-Size Models Are Here!
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Tongyi Lab releases the Qwen3.5 series of small-size models (0.8B to 9B), focusing on lightweight design, high performance, and Apache 2.0 open-source commercial use.

relatedArticles.title: All-in-One Text, Image, and Video! An Open-Source Framework for Multimodal Knowledge Bases
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: Tongyi Lab has open-sourced the VimRAG framework, which leverages Dynamic Acyclic Graphs (DAG) and Graph-Guided Policy Optimization to solve cross-modal retrieval and long-context reasoning challenges in mixed-media knowledge bases.

relatedArticles.title: GPT Image 2 Reclaims the SOTA Throne in Image Generation: A Comprehensive Text-to-Image Evaluation is Here.
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides a comprehensive and in-depth evaluation of ChatGPT's latest image generation model, GPT Image 2, showcasing its significant improvements and existing shortcomings in understanding complex instructions, information density, layout logic, and style consistency through 40 detailed prompts and generated results across 12 design scenarios including infographics, posters, brand VI, game settings, and UI design.

relatedArticles.title: MiniMax Music 2.6: We Want to Tell the Stories of Four People
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article showcases the core capability upgrades of the MiniMax Music 2.6 model in scenarios such as Chinese-style scoring, game music, ambient music, and song adaptation through the real stories of four creators, and introduces the open-source Music Skill tools for developers.

relatedArticles.title: From Transparent Development to Systems Engineering: AgentScope 2.0 Released
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: AgentScope 2.0 upgrades from transparent development to systems engineering, focusing on stable operation, security control, and production-level deployment capabilities for agents in real-world scenarios.
